1. Male or female participants between 18 and 55 years of age (inclusive) at time of consent.
2. Body mass index from 18.0 to 32.0 kg/m2 (inclusive).

3. In good health as determined by: a. Medical history b. Physical examination c. Vital signs d. Neurological examination e. Electrocardiogram f. Serum chemistry, lipid panel, thyroid panel, coagulation panel, urinalysis, hematology, and serology tests (from screening visit).
4. Willing to stay in the clinic for the required period (ie, to be hospitalized) and willing to be contacted for the safety follow-up telephone call.

5. Ability to provide written, informed consent prior to initiation of any trial-related procedures, and ability, in the opinion of the Principal Investigator, to comply with all the requirements of the trial.
2. Have a positive pregnancy test prior to receiving IMP.

3. Participants of reproductive potential (PORP)/ participants of childbearing potential (POCBP) who do not agree to practice 2 different highly effective methods of birth control or remain fully abstinent from sexual activity with the potential for conception, per the guidelines in Section 10.3.
4. Participants who do not agree to refrain from donating sperm or eggs from trial screening through 90 days after the last dose of IMP.

5. Participant has any clinically significant unstable medical condition or any clinically significant chronic disease that in the opinion of the investigator, would limit the participant’s ability to complete and/or participate in the study, including any clinically significant hematological (including deep vein thrombosis) or bleeding disorder, renal, metabolic, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, urological, cardiovascular, hepatic, neurologic or allergic disease (except for untreated seasonal allergies that are asymptomatic at the time of dosing)
6. History of drug and/or alcohol abuse within 2 years prior to screening.

7. History of current hepatitis or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome or carriers of hepatitis B surface antigen and/or hepatitis C antibodies or HIV antibodies. Exceptions are permitted for participants with a prior history of infection with hepatitis A who have fully recovered and are experiencing no liver sequelae, or with hepatitis C who have been adequately treated to be considered cured with no liver sequelae.
8. History of any significant drug allergy or known or suspected hypersensitivity to any component of IMP.
9. A positive urine alcohol test or positive urine drug screen for substances of abuse at screening and upon check-in to the trial site.
10. Any history of significant bleeding or hemorrhagic tendencies.
11. Participant who does not tolerate venipuncture or has poor venous access that would cause difficulty for collecting blood samples.
12. The donation of blood or plasma within 30 days prior to the first dose of IMP.
13. Have taken an investigational drug within 30 days or 5 half-lives, if known, (whichever is longer) prior to screening.
14. Have had previous exposure to SEP-380135.
15. Are currently participating in another clinical trial.

16. Use of any new prescription, over-the-counter, or herbal medications or vitamin supplements including (C and D) or dietary supplements, eg, minerals (calcium, iron), amino acids, enzymes, fish oil (omega-3), probiotics within 14 days prior to the first dose of IMP and oral antibiotics within 30 days prior to the first dose of IMP. The sponsor may allow exceptions only if the medication’s administration is deemed unlikely to impact the PK or PD results.
17. Exposure to any substances known to stimulate hepatic microsomal enzymes within 30 days prior to screening (eg, occupational exposure to pesticides, organic solvents, etc).

18. Use of tobacco products or daily exposure to second- hand smoke within 2 months prior to the screening visit, or urine cotinine concentrations > 200 ng/mL or serum cotinine concentrations > 20 ng/mL at screening or check- in to the trial site.

19. Presenting with, or having a history of, uncontrolled hypertension (systolic blood pressure > 140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure > 90 mmHg in supine position) or symptomatic hypotension or orthostatic hypotension, which is defined as a decrease of >= 20 mmHg in systolic blood pressure and/or a decrease of >= 10 mmHg in diastolic blood pressure after at least 3 minutes of standing compared with the previous supine blood pressure, at screening or check-in. Blood pressure measurements may be repeated once at the discretion of the investigator.

20. Participants who have a supine heart rate, after resting for at least 3 minutes, outside the range of 50 to 100 beats per minute, ie, heart rate: > 100 bpm and< 50 bpm at screening or check-in or predose timepoints. The sponsor may allow exceptions if the results are not considered to be clinically significant; however, this will need to be approved by the medical monitor and sponsor physician. Note: If the first heart rate measurement is abnormal, it can be repeated at the investigator’s discretion, in which case a third (confirmatory) measurement may also be required.

22. Clinically relevant ECG findings at screening or check- in or predose timepoints including heart rate: > 100 bpm and < 50 bpm, QT interval corrected for heart rate using Fridericia’s formula (QTcF) > 450 msec for male participants or > 470 msec for female participants, QRS internal > 120 msec or PR interval > 200 msec. A participant with non-clinically significant ECG abnormalities at screening and check-in requires approval from the medical monitor and the sponsor’s physician.
23. Heavy consumption of alcohol and/or food and beverages containing caffeine and methylxanthines (eg, coffee) within 72 hours prior to dosing.
24. Consumption of foods known to affect cytochrome P450 (CYP) 1A2 (eg,charbroiled or pan-fried meats and cruciferous vegetables) within 72 hours priorto dosing.
25. Consumption of foods or supplements known to inhibit or induce CYP3A4, eg,pomelo, grapefruit, Seville oranges, St. John’s Wort within 72 hours prior todosing.
26. Active suicidal ideation as evidenced by clinical examination or an answer of “yes” on Questions 4 or 5 of

the C-SSRS at screening (ie, in the past 1 month) or prior to dosing at subsequent C-SSRS assessment (ie, since Last Visit version) or suicidal behavior is present in the C- SSRS Since Last Visit version.
27. Attempted suicide within 12 months prior to screening.
28. Are at risk of harming themselves or others according to the investigator’s judgment.

29. A disorder or history of a condition, or previous gastrointestinal conditions or previous gastrointestinal surgery (eg, cholecystectomy, vagotomy, bowel resection) that may interfere with drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, gastrointestinal motility, or pH, or a history of clinically significant abnormality of the hepatic (including participants with moderate [Child-Pugh Class B] and severe [Child-Pugh Class C] hepatic impairment) or renal system (an estimated glomerular filtration rate < 90 mL/min/1.73 m2 at screening only) or a history of malabsorption (appendectomy, and hernia repair will be acceptable), bowel resection, bariatric surgery or gastric band/lap band surgery, or is on medications that might interfere with gastric motility.

30. A history of malignancy within 5 years prior to screening, except for adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, or in situ cervical cancer. Any history of endocrine tumor is excluded.
31. Received active oral, intravenous, or intramuscular steroid treatment 30 days before screening or the first dosing day.

32. A history of sick sinus syndrome, first-, second-, or third- degree atrioventricular block, myocardial infarction, New York Heart Association Class II-IV heart failure, cardiomyopathy, pulmonary congestion, cardiac arrhythmia, prolonged QT interval, congenital long QT syndrome, family history of long QT, or moderate to severe hypokalemia (potassium < 3.0 mmol/L). A participant with non-clinically significant ECG abnormalities at screening and check-in requires approval from the medical monitor and the sponsor’s physician.

33. Participant with aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) >= 3 times the upper limit of the reference ranges provided by the central laboratory at screening or admission. Participant with liver function test for bilirubin >= 2 × upper limit of normal (ULN) at screening or admission.

34. Participant has any clinically significant abnormal laboratory value(s) (hematology, serum chemistry, urinalysis, lipid panel, coagulation panel, and thyroid panel) at screening or admission as judged by the investigator (Note: abnormal findings that may be clinically significant or of questionable significance will be discussed with the medical monitor prior to including subject. Retesting is allowed once during screening and the retest used to determine eligibility).
35. Any type of anemia with hemoglobin <= 11 g/dL.
36. Are a clinical site staff member or the relative of a clinical site staff member.
37. In the opinion of the investigator, should not participate in the trial.
